extracted.intended_audience: computational linguistics / AI researchers and practitioners working on visual storytelling and story generation
extracted.subtask_description: Automatic generation of coherent, engaging stories from image sequences (visual storytelling) by modeling storylines and using iterative refinement. The paper focuses on producing storylines via a story graph and improving final stories with an iterative 'rework' training process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherent and engaging story
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative writers use their knowledge and worldview to put disjointed elements together to form a coherent storyline; writing a coherent and engaging story is a key objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper asserts that automated visual storytelling models struggle to form coherent, engaging narratives from disjointed inputs; the proposed approach (PR-VIST) explicitly aims to form a coherent storyline by modeling and choosing a path through a story graph before generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external knowledge / worldview
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective storytelling leverages external knowledge and a writer's worldview to connect elements into a storyline; lack of such use is a shortcoming of prior automated models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors highlight that VIST models 'make poor use of external knowledge' and imply that leveraging such knowledge is necessary to produce human-like, coherent stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative working and reworking
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers 'work and rework iteratively toward perfection'; iterative generation and refinement is an important production practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR-VIST models this by learning to generate the final story via an iterative training process (reworking), suggesting iterative refinement improves story quality compared to single-pass generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storyline modeling via story graph and best-path plotting
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent the input image sequence as a story graph and find the best path to form a storyline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper's plotting component constructs a story graph from images and searches for an optimal path that serves as the storyline input for generation; this structural plotting step is presented as a production guideline to improve narrative formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity (evaluation metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories should score well on diversity; PR-VIST produces stories 'superior in terms of diversity' according to evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity is reported as one of the quantitative evaluation axes (measured by automatic metrics and human judgments) used to compare models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence (evaluation metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coherence is an explicit evaluation dimension: generated stories should be coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper claims PR-VIST yields superior coherence in both automatic and human evaluations; coherence is targeted by the plotting (storyline) component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanness / human-likeness (evaluation metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated stories should appear human-like ('humanness') in style and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humanness is measured via human evaluation and is cited as a key metric where PR-VIST outperforms baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of both plotting and reworking (component contribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Both plotting (storyline construction) and reworking (iterative generation) contribute to improved story quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ablation study reported in the paper shows that removing either plotting or reworking reduces performance, implying that effective systems should incorporate both components to maximize diversity, coherence, and humanness.
